title: Quotient localizations agree after killing the difference of ideals
statement: Let $k,R$ be commutative rings and $R$ a $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Let $J\subseteq I$ be ideals of $R$ and $A,B\in R$ with $Ax\in J$ for every $x\in I$. Then the principal localizations [def-weil-ring-localization-away] $(R/J)_{\overline{AB}}$ and $(R/I)_{\overline{AB}}$ are isomorphic as $k$-algebras. No nonzero or nontriviality assumption is needed.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci), proof of (2) implies (1), paragraph beginning with clearing the denominators d_i; source checked online and algebra.tex read in the sandbox scratchpad.

proof.text: The quotient factor map R/J to R/I induces a map between the principal localizations, since AB maps to a unit; use Ideal.Quotient.factorₐ and IsLocalization.Away.liftAlgHom.

In the localization of R/J, the product of the images of A and B is a unit, hence A is a unit. For x in I, the image of Ax is zero by the hypothesis. Cancel the unit A to deduce that x maps to zero. Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ therefore supplies a map R/I to the localization of R/J.

The image of AB under that map is a unit, so extend it to the reverse localization map by IsLocalization.Away.liftAlgHom. The two composites fix the image of R, checked using the lift formulas. Quotient.algHom_ext and IsLocalization.algHom_ext imply both composites are identities. AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom gives the claimed equivalence, including the case B=0.

mathlib_searches.query: For ideals J contained in I with A times I contained in J, quotient rings R/J and R/I have isomorphic localizations at the image of A times B
If ideals J and I satisfy J contained in I and A times I contained in J then the localizations of R/J and R/I after inverting A B are isomorphic

theorem nonempty_quotient_away_equiv_of_clearing
    {k : Type u} {R : Type v} [CommRing k] [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    (J I : Ideal R) (hJI : J ≤ I) (A B : R)
    (hclear : ∀ x ∈ I, A * x ∈ J) :
    Nonempty (Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk J (A * B)) ≃ₐ[k]
      Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (A * B)))
